body:
## Goal

Add an opt-in experimental mode that interprets and executes typical natural-language CLI tasks through Formal AI. The existing README describes pattern-based aliases in `substitutions.lino`; this mode must exercise Formal AI's reasoning and tool execution rather than add another catalogue of hardcoded example commands.

Requested syntax:

```sh
$ --use-formal-ai -- print list of files in current directory
```

The `$` above is the installed executable, not a shell prompt. Text after `--` is the user's natural-language request. Accept natural variations, including the original request's spelling “corrent directory”.

## Requirements

- Explicitly opt in with `--use-formal-ai`; preserve ordinary command and existing alias behavior when absent. Pass the full request after `--` to Formal AI without having the shell interpret it as a command.
- Use the current JavaScript Formal AI runtime for the fast development loop, record its exact resolved version/source identity, and preserve JavaScript/Rust CLI behavior parity. Do not silently use an older runtime or fall back to an LLM, alias table, or separately authored shell solution.
- Make Formal AI own interpretation, observation, formalization/decomposition where needed, and tool selection. Execute its tool calls through the existing command runner while preserving working directory, environment policy, isolation, cancellation, stdout/stderr and real exit status.
- Aim to cover typical commands through reusable capabilities: directory listing, file inspection/search, bounded filesystem operations and simple development tasks. Start with the smallest tasks and increase difficulty after independent success. Unsupported or ambiguous requests must terminate with an explicit useful failure/gap and no unintended effects; do not claim universal support from a few examples.
- Bound steps, retries, output, duration and resource use. Preserve existing permissions and effect controls. Referenced/example paths do not grant write authority. Observe a target before editing it; preserve unrelated content and verify actual readback.
- Retain privacy-conscious, inspectable execution evidence: original request, runtime identity, observations, selected tools, process status, effects and remaining obligations. A read, plan, source echo or diagnostic is not a completed mutation. Keep secrets and personal files out of uploaded logs.
- Prefer implementing and improving this feature by giving natural-language tasks to Formal AI itself. Keep failures as regressions. Distinguish source-derived output from supplied implementations or literal copies; externally authored bootstraps must be disclosed and receive no autonomous authorship credit.

## Acceptance

1. Demonstrate the syntax above on an isolated fixture directory and independently compare the observed listing to its actual contents, including spaces and Unicode names. Verify the current directory remains unchanged and no files are modified.
2. Add offline unit tests with actual captured tool receipts for paraphrases, a novel directory/task, missing or ambiguous paths, unsupported operations, failed tools, cancellation, exhausted budgets and malicious instruction-like file contents. Check truthful completion and real exit status.
3. Test parsing of `--`, option-like request text and shell metacharacters so untrusted text is never executed directly as shell syntax. Test no silent fallback when Formal AI is unavailable.
4. Keep real integration/e2e tests available as opt-ins; essential PR checks should be fast, preferably offline Linux JavaScript units. Do not compile or test Rust locally; native/build qualification belongs in CI.
5. Document experimental status, supported/unsupported behavior, installation/runtime resolution, logs, resource controls and reproducible examples. Verify the option in a released CLI before claiming delivery.

Related development: [formal-ai #1483](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1483), [formal-ai PR #1495](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1495), and the ordered coding plan [formal-ai #1170](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1170). This issue records follow-up work in `start`; it does not expand the current Formal AI PR into a second implementation task. 

Please prefer using checks in CI/CD, not on local development machine, so we can minimize our CPU/RAM usage locally, in CI/CD you can test everything you need.

All issues you will find in Formal AI you can report there, in start command itself our main goal is to provide connectivity with Formal AI so once release we can test it more. All previous features should preserve backward compatibility. This is new experimental and optional feature.
title: Experimental --use-formal-ai mode: execute natural-language CLI tasks through Formal AI only
